Its title is almost self-explanatory once one knows the roots: “mother-of-pearl” clouds are not part of its formal taxonomic name, but that luminous, unreal quality is why they fascinate observers. Seen in the far cold of the upper atmosphere, especially near polar regions, they are less common weather than atmospheric apparition. Their scientific category begins not with shape alone, but with an altitude so extreme it almost feels misplaced. What is it?

12. This one is not defined first by texture or rain but by event: it is born from violence, fire, eruption, or detonation rather than ordinary sky-making. Its name combines the idea of a storm-bearing vertical tower with one of heat or flame, and it has accompanied everything from volcanic eruptions to modern warfare. In visual memory, it often looks less like weather than like history becoming visible. What is it?
